```{r sourceData, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

library(lubridate)

library(sf)
library(multimode) #to calculate modes for the age plot
library(findSVI) #for SVI calculation
library(diptest)
library(ggrepel)

# get the most updated data files
source("data_preprocessing/mass_processing.R")
# set working directory -- I have to do this after sourcing the data because it loses the path otherwise
setwd("C:\\Users\\ar2529\\Desktop\\overdose_age")
```

```{r importData, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
female_old <- subset(mass_old, Sex_revised == "Female")

latine_old <- subset(mass_old, Race == "Hispanic")

# get town data from tigris so we can map deaths by town later

options(tigris_use_cache=TRUE)
ma_towns = county_subdivisions(state="Massachusetts")
ma_towns$NAME = str_to_title(ma_towns$NAME)
ma_towns = filter(ma_towns, NAME != "County Subdivisions Not Defined")
# tigris also has shapefiles for the ocean so let's get rid of that
ma_towns <- subset(ma_towns, ALAND!=0)
```

### Age distribution for all fatal and nonfatal overdoses {.tabset}

#### 2009

```{r age2009, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#there was an issue with the x axis not showing up when I coped the other histogram code -- resolved using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42425195/ggplot-data-year-over-year-axis-labels-not-showing

#fixed issue with colors not showing -- turns out it was because the data was numeric: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55400037/ggplot-geom-bar-fill-not-coloring-bars-on-plot

#calculate modes, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27418461/calculate-the-modes-in-a-multimodal-distribution-in-r

# Select an appropriate bandwidth. Here we use a "rule of thumb" method
# looks like there are some NAs in the 2009 data so I have to get rid of them
bandwidth <- bw.nrd0(na.omit(mass_2009$age)) 

# Other methods, e.g. bw.ucv(), will identify different bandwidths as optimal
# Consequently the number (and position) of modes may differ too

# Methods implemented in multimode are documented at ?bw.nrd

# Calculate number of modes
n <- nmodes(mass_2009$age, bw = bandwidth)

# Calculate location of these modes
loc <- locmodes(mass_2009$age, mod0 = n, display=TRUE)
# Remove `, display = TRUE` if you don't want to see the KDE
#loc

# Locations of modes are odd values in loc
modes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 1, by = 2, length.out = n)]
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

# subset out "young" and "old" populations -- "young" is <= first antimode, "old" is > first antimode
mass_2009_young <- subset(mass_2009, age <= antimodes[1])
mass_2009_old <- subset(mass_2009, age > antimodes[1])

# create a condition to use different colors based on the location of the antimode
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13372523/altering-the-color-of-one-value-in-a-ggplot-histogram
# it just gives me a 0 for anything in the younger population, 1 for older

mass_2009$aftermode <- mass_2009$age > antimodes[1]

#added multiple mode lines to plot using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71580196/add-horizontal-lines-from-a-vector-to-a-ggplot-uisng-facet-grid


# a plot without mode lines or anything, with the number of people dying for each age 
ggplot(data=mass_2009, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(aftermode)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 0), breaks = seq(min(mass_2009$age), max(mass_2009$age), by = 5), labels = seq(min(mass_2009$age), max(mass_2009$age), by = 5), minor_breaks = seq(min(mass_2009$age), max(mass_2009$age), by = 1)) + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2009 MA opioid-detected overdose deaths")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of decedents")

age_2009 <- ggplot(data=mass_2009, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(aftermode)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 0), breaks = seq(min(mass_2009$age), max(mass_2009$age), by = 5), labels = seq(min(mass_2009$age), max(mass_2009$age), by = 5), minor_breaks = seq(min(mass_2009$age), max(mass_2009$age), by = 1)) + theme_light() + geom_vline(xintercept = modes, size=1) + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2009 MA opioid-detected overdose deaths")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of decedents")

age_2009

ggsave(plot=age_2009, filename = "images/mass/age_2009.png", width = 10, height = 8)


sprintf("Using Hartigan's dip test for bimodality, the resulting p value is %f.", dip.test(mass_2009$age)$p.value) 

```

```{r age2010, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]
```

```{r age2020White, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Consequently the number (and position) of modes may differ too

# Methods implemented in multimode are documented at ?bw.nrd

# Calculate number of modes
n <- nmodes(white_2020$age, bw = bandwidth)

# Calculate location of these modes
loc <- locmodes(white_2020$age, mod0 = n, display=TRUE)
# Remove `, display = TRUE` if you don't want to see the KDE
#loc

# Locations of modes are odd values in loc
modes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 1, by = 2, length.out = n)]
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

# subset out "young" and "old" populations -- "young" is <= first antimode, "old" is > first antimode
white_2020_young <- subset(white_2020, age <= antimodes[1])
white_2020_old <- subset(white_2020, age > antimodes[1])

#added multiple mode lines to plot using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71580196/add-horizontal-lines-from-a-vector-to-a-ggplot-uisng-facet-grid


# a plot without mode lines or anything, with the number of people dying for each age 
ggplot(data=white_2020, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(age)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = white_2020$age, labels = white_2020$age) + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2020 MA opioid-detected overdose deaths in white people")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))

age_2020

ggsave(plot=age_2020, filename = "images/mass/age_2020_white.png", width = 10, height = 8)
```

```{r age2021Female, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#there was an issue with the x axis not showing up when I coped the other histogram code -- resolved using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42425195/ggplot-data-year-over-year-axis-labels-not-showing

#calculate modes, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27418461/calculate-the-modes-in-a-multimodal-distribution-in-r

# Select an appropriate bandwidth. Here we use a "rule of thumb" method
bandwidth <- bw.nrd0(female_2021$age) 

# Other methods, e.g. bw.ucv(), will identify different bandwidths as optimal
# Consequently the number (and position) of modes may differ too

# Methods implemented in multimode are documented at ?bw.nrd

# Calculate number of modes
n <- nmodes(female_2021$age, bw = bandwidth)

# Calculate location of these modes
loc <- locmodes(female_2021$age, mod0 = n, display=TRUE)
# Remove `, display = TRUE` if you don't want to see the KDE
#loc

# Locations of modes are odd values in loc
modes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 1, by = 2, length.out = n)]
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

# subset out "young" and "old" populations -- "young" is <= first antimode, "old" is > first antimode
female_2021_young <- subset(female_2021, age <= antimodes[1])
female_2021_old <- subset(female_2021, age > antimodes[1])

#added multiple mode lines to plot using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71580196/add-horizontal-lines-from-a-vector-to-a-ggplot-uisng-facet-grid
```

### Race of decedents {.tabset}

#### 2009-2017

**Young**

```{r raceNumericYoung, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
for(i in 1:length(masslistYoung)){
  # get the df you need -- you need the double brackets, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32007076/loop-through-list-of-data-frames
  mass <- masslistYoung[[i]] 
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  year <- mass$Year[1]
  
# see if I can automate the title, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/59095237/automate-ggplots-while-using-variable-labels-as-title-and-axis-titles
racetitle <- paste("Racial distribution for", year, "MA opioid-detected overdose deaths in younger people")

race <- ggplot(data=mass, aes(x=Race, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = Race), position = "dodge")  + scale_fill_manual(name = "Race", values = c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#CC79A7"), labels = c("Black", "Hispanic", "Other", "White")) + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black")+ ggtitle(racetitle)+ theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7)) 

# seem to need to use print() when in a for loop, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/29053223/plots-not-working-in-for-loop
print(race)

# try to automate the filenames? from https://www.edureka.co/community/41963/r-programming-naming-the-output-file-using-a-variable
ggsave(plot=race, filename = paste0("images/mass/race_", year, "_young.png"), width = 10, height = 8)

raceProp <- ggplot(data=mass, aes(x=Race, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = Race), position = "dodge")  + scale_fill_manual(name = "Race", values = c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#CC79A7"), labels = c("Black", "Hispanic", "Other", "White")) + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = round(..count../nrow(mass), 3)), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black")+ ggtitle(racetitle)+ theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))  

print(raceProp)

#save this one for the presentation
ggsave(plot=raceProp, filename = paste0("images/mass/race_proportions_", year, "_young.png"), width = 10, height = 8)
  
}

```

### Chi squared testing for race {.tabset}

#### 2009-2017

```{r chiSquaredRace, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# initialize empty matrix, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32712301/create-empty-data-frame-with-column-names-by-assigning-a-string-vector
# this will hold all the p values

chisq_race <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 2, nrow = 0))
cols <- c("Year", "p value")

for(i in 1:length(masslistYoung)){
  # get the df you need -- you need the double brackets, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32007076/loop-through-list-of-data-frames
  young <- masslistYoung[[i]] 
  old <- masslistOld[[i]] 
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  year <- young$Year[1]
  
  racefreqtable <- young %>% group_by(Race) %>% tally()
  names(racefreqtable)[names(racefreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

  racetableold <- old %>% group_by(Race) %>% tally()
  names(racetableold)[names(racetableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

  racetable <- merge(racefreqtable, racetableold, by="Race")
  
  # convert the "race" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

  racemat <- racetable[,-1]
  rownames(racemat) <- racetable[,1]

  print(as.matrix(racemat))
  
  # append year and p value to a vector, rounding to make it more legible
  results <- c(year, round(chisq.test(as.matrix(racemat))$p.value, 4))
  
  # add this to the chi squared df 
  chisq_race <- rbind(chisq_race, results)

}

# for some reason it doesn't work if I do this before adding rows?
colnames(chisq_race) <- cols

chisq_race

```

#### 2018

```{r chiSquaredRace2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# getting this from https://www.datacamp.com/tutorial/chi-square-test-r

# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

racefreqtable <- mass_2018_young %>% group_by(Race) %>% tally()
names(racefreqtable)[names(racefreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

racetableold <- mass_2018_old %>% group_by(Race) %>% tally()
names(racetableold)[names(racetableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

racetable2018 <- merge(racefreqtable, racetableold, by="Race")

# convert the "race" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

racemat2018 <- racetable2018[,-1]
rownames(racemat2018) <- racetable2018[,1]

as.matrix(racemat2018)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(racemat2018))
```
It looks like there is no significant relationship between age group of decedents and the racial distribution. 

#### 2019

```{r chiSquaredRace2019, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

racefreqtable <- mass_2019_young %>% group_by(Race) %>% tally()
```

```{r chiSquaredRace2021, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
racefreqtable <- mass_2021_young %>% group_by(Race) %>% tally()
names(racefreqtable)[names(racefreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

racetableold <- mass_2021_old %>% group_by(Race) %>% tally()
names(racetableold)[names(racetableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

racetable2021 <- merge(racefreqtable, racetableold, by="Race")

# convert the "race" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

racemat2021 <- racetable2021[,-1]
rownames(racemat2021) <- racetable2021[,1]

as.matrix(racemat2021)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(racemat2021))
```

### Chi squared testing for sex {.tabset}

#### 2009-2017

```{r chiSquaredSex, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# initialize empty matrix, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32712301/create-empty-data-frame-with-column-names-by-assigning-a-string-vector
# this will hold all the p values

chisq_sex <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 2, nrow = 0))
cols <- c("Year", "p value")

for(i in 1:length(masslistYoung)){
  # get the df you need -- you need the double brackets, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32007076/loop-through-list-of-data-frames
  young <- masslistYoung[[i]] 
  old <- masslistOld[[i]] 
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  year <- young$Year[1]
  
  sexfreqtable <- young %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
  names(sexfreqtable)[names(sexfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

  sextableold <- old %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
  names(sextableold)[names(sextableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

  sextable <- merge(sexfreqtable, sextableold, by="Sex_revised")
  
  # convert the "race" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

  sexmat <- sextable[,-1]
  rownames(sexmat) <- sextable[,1]

  print(as.matrix(sexmat))
  
  # append year and p value to a vector, rounding to make it more legible
  results <- c(year, round(chisq.test(as.matrix(sexmat))$p.value, 4))
  
  # add this to the chi squared df 
  chisq_sex <- rbind(chisq_sex, results)

}

# for some reason it doesn't work if I do this before adding rows?
colnames(chisq_sex) <- cols

chisq_sex

```

#### 2018

```{r chiSquaredSex2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

sexfreqtable <- mass_2018_young %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
names(sexfreqtable)[names(sexfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

sextableold <- mass_2018_old %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
names(sextableold)[names(sextableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

sextable2018 <- merge(sexfreqtable, sextableold, by="Sex_revised")

# convert the "sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

sexmat2018 <- sextable2018[,-1]
rownames(sexmat2018) <- sextable2018[,1]

as.matrix(sexmat2018)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(sexmat2018))
```

#### 2019

```{r chiSquaredSex2019, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

sexfreqtable <- mass_2019_young %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
names(sexfreqtable)[names(sexfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

sextableold <- mass_2019_old %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
names(sextableold)[names(sextableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

sextable2019 <- merge(sexfreqtable, sextableold, by="Sex_revised")

# convert the "sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

sexmat2019 <- sextable2019[,-1]
rownames(sexmat2019) <- sextable2019[,1]

as.matrix(sexmat2019)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(sexmat2019))
```

### Race and sex of decedents {.tabset}

#### 2009-2017

**Young**

```{r sexRaceTableYoung, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# create dummy df with race sex info for all years

racesexmat <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 4, nrow = 0))
cols <- c("Year", "Race_sex", "Proportion", "Color")

for(i in 1:length(masslistYoung)){

  # get the df you need -- you need the double brackets, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32007076/loop-through-list-of-data-frames
  mass <- masslistYoung[[i]] 
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  year <- mass$Year[1]

raceSextitle <- paste("Race/ethnicity and sex distribution for", year, "MA opioid-detected \n overdose deaths in younger people")

  
raceSex <- ggplot(data=mass, aes(x=Race_sex, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = Race_sex), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = -0.25, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt)+ ggtitle(raceSextitle)+ theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7)) 

print(raceSex)

ggsave(plot=raceSex, filename = paste0("images/mass/raceSex", year, "_young.png"), width = 10, height = 8)

raceSexProp <- ggplot(data=mass, aes(x=Race_sex, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = Race_sex), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = round(..count../nrow(mass), 3)), stat = "count", vjust = -0.25, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt)+ ggtitle(raceSextitle)+ theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))  

print(raceSexProp)

ggsave(plot=raceSexProp, filename = paste0("images/mass/raceSexProp", year, "_young.png"), width = 10, height = 8)

# get the % of each race sex category
mass <- mass %>% 
  group_by(Race_sex) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(per=`n`/sum(`n`)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(Race_sex))
# create a label out of this
mass$racesexlabel <- scales::percent(mass$per)

# create a year label [for plotting]
mass$Year <- year

# automatically assign the color based on race sex value -- not doing this in preprocessing because I don't want this to be a global change
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39142596/r-ggplot-set-colour-for-specific-value

mass$color <- ifelse(mass$Race_sex == "Black Female", "#e6d0a1", ifelse(mass$Race_sex == "Black Male", "#E69F00", ifelse(mass$Race_sex == "Hispanic Female", "#b3d4e8", ifelse(mass$Race_sex == "Hispanic Male", "#56B4E9", ifelse(mass$Race_sex == "Other Female", "#cca1b9", ifelse(mass$Race_sex == "Other Male", "#CC79A7", ifelse(mass$Race_sex == "White Female", "#a1a1a1", "#000000")))))))

# grab the values i need from nc
results <- select(mass, Year, Race_sex, per, color)
  
# add this to the chi squared df 
racesexmat <- rbind(racesexmat, results)


# plot into a pie chart -- for some reason I have to reverse the colors to get them to work right
piechart <- ggplot(data=mass)+
  geom_bar(aes(x="", y=per, fill=Race_sex), stat="identity", width = 1)+
  coord_polar("y", start=0)+
  theme_void()+ geom_label_repel(aes(label = racesexlabel, x = "", y = cumsum(per) - per/2), nudge_x = 0.02,
                   size = 3, show.legend = F)+  scale_fill_manual(name = "Race/ethnicity and sex", values=rev(mass$color), labels = rev(mass$Race_sex))+ ggtitle(raceSextitle)+ theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right")  
# geom_text(aes(x=1, y = cumsum(per) - per/2, label=label)) for regular labels [not repelling]

print(piechart)

ggsave(plot=piechart, filename = paste0("images/mass/pie", year, "_young.png"), width = 10, height = 8)

}

# for some reason it doesn't work if I do this before adding rows?
colnames(racesexmat) <- cols

#racesexmat


# fill in missing years with NAs so they won't show up interpolated -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65097273/r-how-to-fill-up-missing-year-values-in-a-data-frame
#racesexmat <- racesexmat %>% complete(Year = 2009:2023)

stackedarea <- ggplot(data = racesexmat, aes(x=Year, y=Proportion, fill=Race_sex)) + 
    geom_area(aes(position = 'stack', group = Race_sex))+  scale_fill_manual(name = "Race/ethnicity and sex", values=rev(racesexmat$Color), labels = rev(racesexmat$Race_sex)) + ggtitle("Race/ethnicity and sex distribution for MA opioid-detected \n overdose deaths in younger people")+theme_bw()+ scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = length(yearList))+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right")

print(stackedarea)

ggsave(plot=stackedarea, filename = paste0("images/mass/rs_area__young.png"), width = 10, height = 8)


```

```{r sexRaceTableYoung2019, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
      geom_bar(aes(fill = Race_sex), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = round(..count../nrow(mass_2019_young), 3)), stat = "count", vjust = -0.25, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt)+ ggtitle("Race/ethnicity and sex distribution for 2019 MA opioid-detected \n overdose deaths in younger people")+ theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))  

raceSexProp2019

ggsave(plot=raceSexProp2019, filename = "images/mass/raceSexProp2019_young.png", width = 10, height = 8)

# pie chart info from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/45657990/how-to-create-a-pie-chart-with-percentage-labels-using-ggplot2

# ggrepel info from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69715282/how-to-adjust-ggrepel-label-on-pie-chart

# get the % of each race sex category
mass_2019_younglong <- mass_2019_young %>% 
  group_by(Race_sex) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(per=`n`/sum(`n`)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(Race_sex))
# create a label out of this
mass_2019_younglong$racesexlabel <- scales::percent(mass_2019_younglong$per)


# automatically assign the color based on race sex value
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39142596/r-ggplot-set-colour-for-specific-value

mass_2019_younglong$color <- ifelse(mass_2019_younglong$Race_sex == "Black Female", "#e6d0a1", ifelse(mass_2019_younglong$Race_sex == "Black Male", "#E69F00", ifelse(mass_2019_younglong$Race_sex == "Hispanic Female", "#b3d4e8", ifelse(mass_2019_younglong$Race_sex == "Hispanic Male", "#56B4E9", ifelse(mass_2019_younglong$Race_sex == "Other Female", "#cca1b9", ifelse(mass_2019_younglong$Race_sex == "Other Male", "#CC79A7", ifelse(mass_2019_younglong$Race_sex == "White Female", "#a1a1a1", "#000000")))))))


# plot into a pie chart -- for some reason I have to reverse the color and labels
pie2019young <- ggplot(data=mass_2019_younglong)+
  geom_bar(aes(x="", y=per, fill=Race_sex), stat="identity", width = 1)+
  coord_polar("y", start=0)+
  theme_void()+ geom_label_repel(aes(label = racesexlabel, x = "", y = cumsum(per) - per/2), nudge_x = 0.02,
                   size = 3, show.legend = F)+  scale_fill_manual(name = "Race/ethnicity and sex", values = rev(mass_2019_younglong$color), labels = rev(mass_2019_younglong$Race_sex)) + ggtitle("Race/ethnicity and sex distribution for 2019 MA opioid-detected overdose deaths in younger people") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right") 
# geom_text(aes(x=1, y = cumsum(per) - per/2, label=label)) for regular labels [not repelling]

pie2019young

ggsave(plot=pie2019young, filename = "images/mass/pie2019_young.png", width = 10, height = 8)
```

### Chi squared testing for race and sex {.tabset}

#### 2009-2017

```{r chiSquaredRaceSex, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# initialize empty matrix, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32712301/create-empty-data-frame-with-column-names-by-assigning-a-string-vector
# this will hold all the p values

chisq_racesex <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 2, nrow = 0))
cols <- c("Year", "p value")

for(i in 1:length(masslistYoung)){
  # get the df you need -- you need the double brackets, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32007076/loop-through-list-of-data-frames
  young <- masslistYoung[[i]] 
  old <- masslistOld[[i]] 
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  year <- young$Year[1]
  
  racesexfreqtable <- young %>% group_by(Race_sex) %>% tally()
  names(racesexfreqtable)[names(racesexfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

  racesextableold <- old %>% group_by(Race_sex) %>% tally()
  names(racesextableold)[names(racesextableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

  racesextable <- merge(racesexfreqtable, racesextableold, by="Race_sex")
  
  # convert the "race" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

  racesexmat <- racesextable[,-1]
  rownames(racesexmat) <- racesextable[,1]

  print(as.matrix(racesexmat))
  
  # append year and p value to a vector, rounding to make it more legible
  results <- c(year, round(chisq.test(as.matrix(racesexmat))$p.value, 4))
  
  # add this to the chi squared df 
  chisq_racesex <- rbind(chisq_racesex, results)

}

# for some reason it doesn't work if I do this before adding rows?
colnames(chisq_racesex) <- cols

chisq_racesex

```

    

#### 2018

```{r chiSquaredRaceSex2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

racesexfreqtable <- mass_2018_young %>% group_by(Race_sex) %>% tally()
names(racesexfreqtable)[names(racesexfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

racesextableold <- mass_2018_old %>% group_by(Race_sex) %>% tally()
names(racesextableold)[names(racesextableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

racesextable2018 <- merge(racesexfreqtable, racesextableold, by="Race_sex")

# convert the "Race_sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

racesexmat2018 <- racesextable2018[,-1]
rownames(racesexmat2018) <- racesextable2018[,1]

as.matrix(racesexmat2018)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(racesexmat2018))
```

### Day of week {.tabset}

#### 2009-2017

**Young**

```{r weekYoung, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
for(i in 1:length(masslistYoung)){

  # get the df you need -- you need the double brackets, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32007076/loop-through-list-of-data-frames
  mass <- masslistYoung[[i]] 
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  year <- mass$Year[1]

weekdaytitle <- paste("ODs per weekday for", year, "MA opioid-detected overdose deaths in younger people")

  
# ordering of variables on x axis from https://www.statology.org/ggplot-order-x-axis/
# make sure to use scale_x_discrete!

weekday <- ggplot(data=mass, aes(x=factor(Weekday, level=c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday")), ..count..)) + geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(Weekday)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 0), breaks = mass$Weekday, labels = mass$Weekday) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black") + ggtitle(weekdaytitle)+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))+xlab("Weekday")

print(weekday)

ggsave(plot=weekday, filename = paste0("images/mass/weekday_", year, "_young.png"), width = 10, height = 8)


weekday_prop <- ggplot(data=mass, aes(x=factor(Weekday, level=c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday")), round(..count../nrow(mass), 3))) + geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(Weekday)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 0), breaks = mass$Weekday, labels = mass$Weekday) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = round(..count../nrow(mass), 3)), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black") + ggtitle(weekdaytitle)+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))+xlab("Weekday")+ylab("Proportion")
```

```{r weekOld, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
  year <- mass$year[1]
```

### Chi squared testing for day of week {.tabset}

#### 2009-2017

```{r chiSquaredWeekday, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# initialize empty matrix, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32712301/create-empty-data-frame-with-column-names-by-assigning-a-string-vector
# this will hold all the p values

chisq_weekday <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 2, nrow = 0))
cols <- c("Year", "p value")

for(i in 1:length(masslistYoung)){
  # get the df you need -- you need the double brackets, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32007076/loop-through-list-of-data-frames
  young <- masslistYoung[[i]] 
  old <- masslistOld[[i]] 
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  year <- young$Year[1]
  
  weekdayfreqtable <- young %>% group_by(Weekday) %>% tally()
  names(weekdayfreqtable)[names(weekdayfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

  weekdaytableold <- old %>% group_by(Weekday) %>% tally()
  names(weekdaytableold)[names(weekdaytableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

  weekdaytable <- merge(weekdayfreqtable, weekdaytableold, by="Weekday")
  
  # convert the "race" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

  weekdaymat <- weekdaytable[,-1]
  rownames(weekdaymat) <- weekdaytable[,1]

  print(as.matrix(weekdaymat))
  
  # append year and p value to a vector, rounding to make it more legible
  results <- c(year, round(chisq.test(as.matrix(weekdaymat))$p.value, 4))
  
  # add this to the chi squared df 
  chisq_weekday <- rbind(chisq_weekday, results)

}

# for some reason it doesn't work if I do this before adding rows?
colnames(chisq_weekday) <- cols

chisq_weekday

```

```{r chiSquaredWeekday2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# convert the "Race_sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

rownames(weekdaymat2018) <- weekdaytable2018[,1]
```

### Chi squared testing for month {.tabset}

#### 2009-2017

```{r chiSquaredMonth, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# initialize empty matrix, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32712301/create-empty-data-frame-with-column-names-by-assigning-a-string-vector
# this will hold all the p values

chisq_month <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 2, nrow = 0))
cols <- c("Year", "p value")

for(i in 1:length(masslistYoung)){
  # get the df you need -- you need the double brackets, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32007076/loop-through-list-of-data-frames
  young <- masslistYoung[[i]] 
  old <- masslistOld[[i]] 
  # grab the year -- you only need the first element in the year column since all of them have the same value
  year <- young$Year[1]
  
  monthfreqtable <- young %>% group_by(Month) %>% tally()
  names(monthfreqtable)[names(monthfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

  monthtableold <- old %>% group_by(Month) %>% tally()
  names(monthtableold)[names(monthtableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

  monthtable <- merge(monthfreqtable, monthtableold, by="Month")
  
  # convert the "race" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

  monthmat <- monthtable[,-1]
  rownames(monthmat) <- monthtable[,1]

  print(as.matrix(monthmat))
  
  # append year and p value to a vector, rounding to make it more legible
  results <- c(year, round(chisq.test(as.matrix(monthmat))$p.value, 4))
  
  # add this to the chi squared df 
  chisq_month <- rbind(chisq_month, results)

}

# for some reason it doesn't work if I do this before adding rows?
colnames(chisq_month) <- cols

chisq_month

```

```{r chiSquaredMonth2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

names(monthfreqtable)[names(monthfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

names(monthtableold)[names(monthtableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

# convert the "Race_sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

monthmat2018 <- monthtable2018[,-1]
rownames(monthmat2018) <- monthtable2018[,1]

as.matrix(monthmat2018)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(monthmat2018))
```

### Proportion of deaths involving synthetic narcotics


```{r propFent, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# unfortunately there are different variable names for each mass file so a for loop won't work :/

# get proportion of fent for each year for younger people -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28195996/count-number-of-rows-matching-a-criteria
fentyoung <- c(sum(mass_2009_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2009_young), sum(mass_2010_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2010_young), sum(mass_2011_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2011_young), sum(mass_2012_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2012_young), sum(mass_2013_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2013_young), sum(mass_2014_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2014_young), sum(mass_2017_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2017_young), sum(mass_2018_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2018_young), sum(mass_2019_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2019_young), sum(mass_2020_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2020_young), sum(mass_2021_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2021_young), sum(mass_2022_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2022_young), sum(mass_2023_young$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2023_young))

# get proportion for older people
fentold <- c(sum(mass_2009_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2009_old), sum(mass_2010_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2010_old), sum(mass_2011_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2011_old), sum(mass_2012_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2012_old), sum(mass_2013_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2013_old), sum(mass_2014_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2014_old), sum(mass_2017_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2017_old), sum(mass_2018_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2018_old), sum(mass_2019_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2019_old), sum(mass_2020_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2020_old), sum(mass_2021_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2021_old), sum(mass_2022_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2022_old), sum(mass_2023_old$synthetic == 1)/nrow(mass_2023_old))

# combine vectors into df
propfent <- data.frame(yearList, fentyoung, fentold)

# change the col names to be more informative
names(propfent) <- c("Year", "Younger", "Older")

# create grouped bar plot, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72449952/making-a-grouped-bar-chart-in-r
# getting the labels in the right position from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37587288/ggplot-label-bars-in-grouped-bar-plot
# info on changing legend title from here https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41649929/how-to-modify-a-legend-title-in-a-barplot-with-ggplot
# the scale x continuous is there because for some reason adding 2023 data messed up the x axis, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72051789/how-to-display-all-values-on-x-and-y-axes-in-r-ggplot2

# increasing line size from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14794599/how-to-change-line-width-in-ggplot
# line graph info from https://www.sthda.com/english/wiki/ggplot2-line-plot-quick-start-guide-r-software-and-data-visualization


pfentlong  <- propfent |>
  # Reshape data to long format
  pivot_longer(Younger:Older)

# create labels with the value of each proportion
pfentlong$labels <- round(pfentlong$value, 2)

pfent <-  ggplot(data = pfentlong, aes(x = Year, y = value, fill = name, group=name, color=factor(name))) +
  # Implement a grouped bar chart
  # Implement a line graph
  geom_line(stat = "identity", size = 1) + geom_point(size = 2) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Proportion of synthetic opioid-detected overdose deaths in MA \n by age group, 2009-2023") + ylab("Proportion") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + scale_fill_discrete(guide="none") + scale_x_continuous(breaks=propfent$Year) + xlab("Year")+ coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) + guides(color = guide_legend(title = "Age group"))+ geom_label_repel(aes(label = labels, x = Year, y = value), nudge_x = 0.1, na.rm = FALSE, color = "black", size = 2.5, label.size = NA, fill = NA)

pfent

ggsave(plot=pfent, filename = "images/mass/prop_synthetic.png", width = 10, height = 8)

```

### Chi squared testing for the number of stimulant-detected deaths

```{r chiSquaredStim, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

# get proportion of stim for each year for younger people -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28195996/count-number-of-rows-matching-a-criteria
stimyoungcount <- c(sum(mass_2009_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2010_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2011_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2012_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2013_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2014_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2017_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2018_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2019_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2020_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2021_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2022_young$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2023_young$stimulant == 1))

# get proportion for older people
stimoldcount <-  c(sum(mass_2009_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2010_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2011_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2012_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2013_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2014_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2017_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2018_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2019_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2020_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2021_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2022_old$stimulant == 1), sum(mass_2023_old$stimulant == 1))

# combine vectors into df
stimcount <- data.frame(yearList, stimyoungcount, stimoldcount)

# change the col names to be more informative
names(stimcount) <- c("Year", "Younger", "Older")

# convert the "Race_sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

stimchi <- stimcount[,-1]
rownames(stimchi) <- stimcount[,1]

as.matrix(stimchi)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(stimchi))

```

```{r chiSquaredEtoh, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
etoholdcount <-  c(sum(mass_2009_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2010_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2011_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2012_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2013_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2014_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2017_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2018_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2019_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2020_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2021_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2022_old$etoh == 1), sum(mass_2023_old$etoh == 1))

# combine vectors into df
etohcount <- data.frame(yearList, etohyoungcount, etoholdcount)

# change the col names to be more informative
names(etohcount) <- c("Year", "Younger", "Older")

# convert the "Race_sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

etohchi <- etohcount[,-1]
rownames(etohchi) <- etohcount[,1]

as.matrix(etohchi)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(etohchi))
```
